note: Before/after a single change: padding the shared output-accumulator row stride from 64 to 65 to break a 16-way bank conflict. Same kernel otherwise.

interpretation.delta: One padding line cut shared store-conflicts 12x (552M -> 46M) and load-conflicts 4.4x, raising SM throughput 3.4x and cutting kernel time 3.4x (45.3 -> 13.3 ms). Correctness unchanged (max abs err ~1e-3 vs a float64 reference).
interpretation.vs_v1: Relative to the fp32 SIMT v1, the WMMA rewrite already collapsed registers/thread 164 -> 64 and doubled occupancy 12% -> 27% by moving the accumulators into fragments.
interpretation.remaining_bottleneck: Even after the fix, tensor-core (HMMA) utilization is only 2% and short-scoreboard (shared/MIO) stalls still dominate at 12.5/issue. The matmuls are a small slice of the runtime; the serial per-row online-softmax glue -- 16 of 32 lanes, scalar shared-memory reductions between the two matmuls -- is what remains. Tensor cores accelerate the matmuls, but attention is not only matmuls; beating a tuned SIMT kernel needs warp-shuffle softmax reductions and K/V reuse across the key loop, the direction a v3 would take. An honest result: v2 is 3.4x faster than the naive WMMA version but does not yet beat v1 or the production mem-efficient kernel.
